title: Adani Green H1: Capacity Up 24% to 20,763 MW, Energy Sales Jump 32%
excerpt: The renewables major added 4,083 MW of greenfield capacity and commissioned 3,081 MWh of battery storage at Khavda; the board meets October 21 to approve Q2 results.
body:
• Adani Green Energy's operational capacity rose 24% year-on-year to 20,763 MW in H1FY27, with energy sales up 32% to 25,747 million units, the company reported on October 10.
  • The company added 4,083 MW of greenfield capacity in the half-year, including 621 MW in the September quarter, and operationalised 3,081 MWh of battery storage at Khavda — taking total storage to 6,632 MWh.
  • The portfolio now comprises 14,550 MW of solar, 2,947 MW of wind, and 3,266 MW of hybrid projects, with strong plant availability across all segments.
  • What it means for you: the board meets on Wednesday, October 21, to approve Q2FY27 results — the key date for shareholders. Shares closed at Rs 1,255.80 on the NSE, up 1.63%, and are up 22.41% in 2026 against a Nifty that has declined nearly 14%.

Adani Green Energy reported a 24% year-on-year rise in operational capacity to 20,763 MW in the first half of FY27, while energy sales jumped 32% to 25,747 million units, supported by capacity additions across its solar, wind, and hybrid portfolio.

The company added 4,083 MW of greenfield capacity during the April–September period, including 621 MW in the second quarter. During the September quarter, it operationalised 3,081 MWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at Khavda in Gujarat, taking total installed storage to 6,632 MWh as of September 30. The Khavda storage deployment — spread across three subsidiaries — accounts for more than half of India's operational battery storage capacity.

AGEL said its operational portfolio powered more than 4.4 million homes and helped avoid 17.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions during the first half.

Context & Background

The scale-up is centered on Khavda, where the company is developing one of the world's largest renewable energy plants across 538 square kilometers of barren land in Gujarat. The BESS additions use lithium-ion technology with energy management systems and automated telemetry to manage charging and discharging — infrastructure meant to steady the grid, manage peak demand, and cut renewable curtailment by delivering power when it is needed.

Generation performance held up across segments. The solar portfolio recorded a capacity utilisation factor of 22.9% with plant availability of 99.3%; wind posted 42.9% CUF with 94.6% availability; and the hybrid portfolio delivered 45.2% CUF with 98.8% availability.

Impact & Analysis

The operational update — provisional, covering the six months ended September 30 — reinforces AGEL's position as India's largest renewable energy company by capacity. The 32% jump in energy sales outpaced the 24% capacity growth, reflecting both new commissioning and strong availability.

The company also collected a fresh round of recognition: it was ranked number one globally in the Alternative Electricity Subsector by FTSE Russell for the second consecutive year, its Khavda storage project received the Largest Project of the Year Award at IESW 2026, and it won the Clean Power Generation Award at the Reuters Energy Industry Awards 2026 in New York. It was also ranked first in its sector by CRISIL for the fifth straight year and received a CareEdge-ESG 1+ rating with a score of 87.3 — the highest ever assigned across sectors, the company said.

Shares settled at Rs 1,255.80 on the NSE, up 1.63% on the day, in a range of Rs 1,238.40 to Rs 1,275. The stock's 52-week range is Rs 765 to Rs 1,631.50, and at the current price the company's market capitalisation stands at about Rs 2.07 lakh crore.

What's Next

The board of directors will meet on October 21, 2026, to consider and approve the unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30. Investors will watch the numbers for confirmation that the capacity surge is translating into revenue and margin growth — revenue from power supply rose 29% year-on-year in Q1FY27 — and for any update on the pace of commissioning toward the company's long-term targets.
